A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDCM work and are readable, including figures and equations. v1 ends after its references despite unresolved supplementary references; v4 supplies Appendices A–C. This is a difference in the supplied documents, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, image-compression, inverse-problem, and face-restoration experiments in Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and supplies additional quantitative and qualitative results, including compressed guidance and image editing.

M1.justification: The central sampler, compression rule, and restoration procedures in Eqs. (5)–(12) remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 adds an explicit adapted alternative to timestep skipping: retain 1000 denoising steps but use singleton codebooks outside steps 400–899. The detailed compressed-guidance and editing descriptions mostly elaborate applications already announced in v1.

E1.justification: v4 adds a concrete qualitative editing evaluation on modified-ImageNetR-TI2I (Appendix C.7, Figure 27), extending demonstrated coverage beyond v1's brief announcement of editing. The principal generation, compression, inverse-problem, and four face-restoration datasets were already specified in v1; additional face results and resolution settings do not constitute new datasets.

E2.justification: The main compression and restoration comparator sets are retained. The supplementary editing comparison adds DDPM inversion and full and mid-way DDIM inversion. Appendices C.5–C.6 also explicitly compare compressed guidance against standard CG and CFG, extending the reported comparisons without replacing the original baseline suite.

E3.justification: Newly reported evaluations introduce 768×768 compression, controlled timestep-selection comparisons, caption-conditioned compression at CFG scales 3 and 6, and compressed-guidance parameter sweeps. Generation evaluation expands to KID and DINOv2 distances, while text guidance adds CLIP alignment assessment. These substantially broaden evaluation design; newly disclosed configurations for retained experiments do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's codebook-size experiment and brief statement about prompts, v4 supplies direct analyses of ordinary versus adapted timestep reduction (B.4, Figure 15), caption conditioning (B.6, Figure 16), and guidance-strength/subset-size tradeoffs (C.5–C.6). These provide substantive evidence about design choices, sensitivity, and quality–fidelity tradeoffs.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly displays shaded ranges around KID and DINOv2 kernel-distance curves, whereas v1's generation plots show unbanded estimates. The text does not define these ranges or report repeated-run counts or seeds, so their confidence level and estimation procedure cannot be determined.

E6.justification: The main results are retained, while the appendices add substantial quantitative and qualitative evidence. Table 8 newly reports CCG FID 13.669 versus standard CG values 31.548, 14.481, and 14.921 under its stated setup; Figure 26 reports lower prompt alignment for CCFG. Additional results cover 768×768 compression and the other face datasets. Tables 2–5 tabulate existing Figure 5 results rather than demonstrating new performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 states Proposition 6.1 and mathematical connections without supplying the referenced proofs. v4 adds a general-SDE proof argument in C.1, derives the approximate compression connection using Gaussian norm concentration in C.2, and develops the MMSE-based restoration objective in C.4.1. The proposition's main-text statement remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: finite codebooks preserve generation quality, enable perceptual compression, and support compressed conditional generation with a posterior-sampling interpretation. Guidance and editing were already announced in v1. The new tokenization discussion is a perspective and future direction rather than a demonstrated core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations concerning unreliable classifier gradients, random-subset selection for diversity, and the rate–perception–distortion interpretation of reduced prompt alignment. It discusses when editing's weaker structural preservation can be useful and interprets codebook indices as autoregressive image tokens. Existing limitations concerning the VAE, high bit rates, and incomplete theoretical understanding remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 1 disclose checkpoint identifiers, codebook sizes, timestep counts, matching-pursuit settings and normalization, and comparator configurations. Further additions specify caption generation and bit accounting, metric implementations, restoration sampler settings, and guidance/editing parameters. These substantially improve reproducibility; the project code/demo link was already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused comparison with Liu et al. (2021), distinguishing its entropy-constrained optimal-transport formulation from DDCM's cross-modal conditioning. The appendices add relevant editing, classifier-robustness, and evaluation references. The broader positioning around discrete diffusion generation and zero-shot compression remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section order, abstract, and much of the exposition are retained. v4 repairs unresolved appendix references, expands selected explanations, adds an impact statement and organized supplementary sections, and updates the publication footer. This is limited editorial revision of the existing narrative despite substantial added scientific material.

P2.justification: v4 adds extensive visual evidence and tabulation: Figures 8–27 and Tables 1–8 include metric plots, comparison grids, configurations, numerical results, and editing examples. Tables 2–5 redisplay existing compression results. Existing Figures 6–7 move, and Figure 5 refines its encoder-decoder-bound labeling and layout.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially remedies v1's missing supporting material: the appendices provide implementable configurations, mathematical arguments, and actual evaluations for previously announced applications, including unfavorable tradeoffs. This materially improves reproducibility and critical assessment while retaining the original evidence. Limitations remain: Figure 8's bands are undefined, and C.1 does not establish why rescaling the diffusion coefficient preserves the claimed posterior.
